Exact bottleneck size estimation

Source: R/bottleneck-exact.R
exactBottleneck.Rd

Estimates transmission bottleneck size using one of three methods:

exact_bb

Beta-binomial likelihood over the number of transmitted variant virions, which models finite recipient read depth, in the spirit of Sobel Leonard et al. (2017). Requires altCount and totalDepth assays. Two deviations from the published method are deliberate: when all or none of the transmitted virions carry the variant, the recipient read counts are modelled with a fixed sequencing error probability of threshold / 2, and the recipient detection threshold is not integrated out. The likelihood needs the recipient's read depth at each donor variant, so it cannot use a site where that depth is unknown: such a site would add the same constant at every Nb. This includes every site that the recipient's VCF file does not list, so with objects read from VCF files a donor variant the recipient lacks usually enters exact_bb not at all, and loss in transmission is then scored only by the other estimators. Such sites are left out, with a message, and counted in n_excluded, not in n_variants; a bootstrap interval (nboot > 0) resamples only the sites used. Where the depth is known but the recipient's alternative count is not, as in an iVar table without ALT_DP, the count is round(altFreq * totalDepth); where the recipient has no frequency there either, it has no call, and the count is 0.

wright_fisher

Approximate score in which one generation of binomial drift is combined with a beta kernel of concentration max(Nb, 2) around the drifted frequency. It mixes a density for detected variants with probabilities for lost variants, so it is a heuristic rather than a likelihood; prefer exact_bb or presence_absence for inference. Like presence_absence, it uses the donor variants with frequencies from threshold to 1 - threshold.

presence_absence

Presence-absence likelihood using \(P(\mathrm{detect} | Nb, \nu) = 1 - (1-\nu)^{Nb}\). As in the published method, it uses the donor variants with frequencies from threshold to 1 - threshold, and leaves out, with a message, those above: a donor variant at frequency 1 that the recipient lacks would have probability 0 under every Nb.

Usage

exactBottleneck(
  whe,
  pairId,
  maxNb = 500L,
  method = c("exact_bb", "wright_fisher", "presence_absence"),
  nboot = 0L,
  threshold = 0.03
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment with transmission pairs defined in colData.

pairId

Character. Which pair to estimate.

maxNb

Integer. Maximum bottleneck size to evaluate (default: 500); a single whole number of at least 1.

method

Character. One of "exact_bb", "wright_fisher", or "presence_absence".

nboot

Integer. Number of bootstrap replicates for confidence intervals (default: 0, uses a likelihood-ratio interval). Bootstrapping resamples variant sites and uses the random number generator, so set a seed for reproducible intervals.

threshold

Numeric. Variant calling threshold (default: 0.03), a single number above 0 and below 0.5: at 0 every recipient frequency counts as present, and from 0.5 no donor variant lies between threshold and 1 - threshold.

Value

A named list with components:

Nb

Numeric. Maximum likelihood estimate of bottleneck size over the grid 1:maxNb. A warning is issued when the estimate reaches maxNb, because the value is then censored by the grid.

ci

Numeric vector of length 2. 95% confidence interval (likelihood-ratio or bootstrap percentile), also bounded by maxNb.

loglik

Numeric. Log-likelihood at the MLE; for "wright_fisher", the heuristic score at its maximiser.

method

Character. Method used. For "wright_fisher" the Nb and ci are the maximiser and interval of a heuristic score, and a message says so when the method is run.

n_variants

Integer. Number of donor variants used.

n_excluded

Named integer. Donor variants at or above threshold that were left out, by reason: recipient_failed_qc, sites where QC removed a recipient call at or above threshold, which is not an absence (see asViralBottleneckInput), left out by every method; unknown_depth, sites of unknown recipient depth, which only exact_bb leaves out; and donor_near_fixation, donor variants above 1 - threshold, which presence_absence and wright_fisher leave out, as quickBottleneck does.

pair_id

Character. Pair identifier.

Details

Every method stops with an error when its log-likelihood is not finite at any Nb of the grid, where it would otherwise return Nb = 1.

References

Sobel Leonard A et al. (2017). Transmission Bottleneck Size Estimation from Pathogen Deep-Sequencing Data, with an Application to Human Influenza A Virus. J Virol 91:e00171-17. doi:10.1128/JVI.00171-17

Examples

vcf1 <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
vcf2 <- system.file("extdata", "test_recipient.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(c(vcf1, vcf2),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("donor", "recipient"),
        role = c("donor", "recipient"),
        pair_id = c("p1", "p1")),
    caller = "ivar")
exactBottleneck(whe, pairId = "p1", maxNb = 50L,
    method = "presence_absence")
#> $Nb
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $ci
#> [1] 1 4
#> 
#> $loglik
#> [1] -5.315958
#> 
#> $method
#> [1] "presence_absence"
#> 
#> $n_variants
#> [1] 15
#> 
#> $n_excluded
#> recipient_failed_qc       unknown_depth donor_near_fixation 
#>                   0                   0                   0 
#> 
#> $pair_id
#> [1] "p1"
#>
